$comment: Derived artifacts of spec inputs (T0012). A task whose allowed_scope covers a marker input MUST also cover the derived artifact: pre-dispatch scope validation fails the spawn otherwise, and collect treats the derived artifact of a covered marker as in scope (so a Worker can regenerate it without an out-of-scope rejection). The pairs mirror scripts/speclib.py derive_spec_version: inputs are tasks/tasks.json plus every file under specs/ except the marker itself.

rules.note: every spec file is an input of the derived spec version marker
the task DAG is an input of the derived spec version marker

The canonical schema snapshot is generated from the migration history (scripts/gen_schema_snapshot.py). It is a derived artifact, not a product spec a Worker edits by judgement: a task whose scope covers infra/migrations/** regenerates it mechanically, and CI fails when the two diverge. This is the auditable path for schema evolution, and it is the whole of the Worker's access to specs/.

The sqlc output (sqlc.yaml: schema infra/migrations, queries internal/persistence/queries). Checked in, regenerated by scripts/gen_sqlc.sh, and CI fails when it drifts (tests/integration/check-sqlc-drift.sh). It is declared so the artifact is REGENERATED rather than merged as text: a task and main both regenerate it, and their two copies differ on every line the other one added, so a textual apply refuses on context alone even when the changes are nowhere near each other — T0209's querier.go, where the task's rsg query methods and main's policy methods interleave alphabetically. The marker is the queries directory and not infra/migrations/** even though the migrations are the other input: sqlc models a table only when some checked-in query reads it, so a migration that adds new tables — nothing queries them yet — leaves this output byte-identical (measured 2026-09-15: adding a table moves nothing). Requiring every migration task to cover it would therefore be an obligation over a thing that did not move, and it would fail the scope check for every task that carries infra/migrations/** today. But a migration that ALTERS an existing table which a checked-in query does read DOES move it — the same pair of experiments: one column added to research_assets, which queries/releases_assets.sql reads, moved models.go and releases_assets.sql.go. A task carrying that kind of migration must also carry internal/persistence/sqlc/**; T0701 (00064) is the case that proved it, and its scope line landed in the same commit as this note. check-sqlc-drift is what catches the class — at CI, on the merge that made it true, provided the generator is actually on the runner: drift_test.go self-skips without the sqlc binary, and the migration-integration job only installs the pinned version since 2026-09-15.
